# Project: Master/Caster of Magic tooling

## Document tiers

| Document | Tier | Write authority |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | CONTRACT | Agents propose changes via `PROPOSALS.md`; they do not edit it. |
| `TASKS.md` | TASKS | Items are added only on explicit approval in conversation. Deleted freely. |
| `TESTS.md` | registry | Agents maintain it. Adding or deleting a `scaffolding` suite is free; promoting one to `spec` or `regression` requires a proposal. |
| `JOURNAL.md` | JOURNAL | Written and pruned freely. Never authoritative, and never cited as justification for a decision. |
| `PROPOSALS.md` | channel | Agents append entries. Only the user merges, edits or deletes them. |

## Source routing

<!-- Anything that binds the design and cannot be discovered by reading the code. -->

Authority rules: binaries outrank prose. For the modern versions, Warlord `.CAS` scripts outrank the compiled behaviour they overwrite, and `UNITS.INI` is authoritative for the roster. The DOS versions have neither scripts nor `UNITS.INI`; for those the binary is the only source.

`C:\ReMoM`, the external MoM reconstruction, ships no licence file and is therefore never vendored into this repository. It never outranks the executable.

Each modern version ships its own `MASTER.CAS`, with version-specific numeric ids.

Where to start reading for a given subject:

| Subject | Start here |
|---|---|
| MoM 1.31 / 1.60 / CoM1 compiled behaviour | `Reference docs/DOS reconstructed/README.md`; `Reference docs/MoM binary analysis.md` is the broader index |
| CoM2 / Warlord compiled behaviour | `Reference docs/Caster binary/CoM2 binary analysis.md`, whose subsystem index routes to the address-backed Pascal reconstructions |
| Warlord scripted behaviour | `Reference docs/Script source/Warlord 1.5.12.7/` |
| CoM2 / Warlord constants | `Reference docs/CoM2 data tables.md`; `UNITS.INI` separately owns roster data |
| DOS rosters | the versioned text sources under `Unit rosters/` |
| Manuals and helptext | the version-matched files under `Reference docs/` |
| Unresolved evidence | `Reference docs/Engine verification evidence.md` |
| Script-versus-prose conflicts | `Reference docs/Source discrepancies.md` |
| Tooltip wording | `Reference docs/Tooltip style guide.md` |

Modern sources compose: compiled code supplies the control flow, INI files supply the runtime
constants, and Warlord scripts may add to or overwrite the result.

## Protocol for execution of TASK items

Every `TASKS.md` item is executed under this protocol, including items that move no numbers.

By default, task items should be executed in a collaboration between a Claude agent and a GPT agent. The preferred agents are Claude Opus 5 on High effort and GPT 5.6 Sol on High reasoning.

By default, tasks should be executed according to method A. Tasks that involve source code reconstruction from the game binaries must be performed with method B. The methods run per subtask, not per item.

### Shape of TASKS.md

T-1. **Items are pre-split into subtasks at filing time.** Each subtask is sized to be carried out
   in one agent prompt, and the item lists them. Work that cannot be stated as one prompt is not
   yet a subtask; split it further before filing.
T-2. **The priority list is one row per subtask.** `TASKS.md` opens with an ordered list naming
   every subtask individually. A row naming two or more subtasks, or a range such as
   `T2.11`–`T2.13`, is malformed.
T-3. **A subtask appears in the list before any subtask that depends on it.** The list is the
   execution order; the item bodies below it are not a queue.

### Method A:
Perform the task implementation using the current agent, then launch another agent to review the work. If the current agent is a Claude agent, the review agent should be a GPT agent; if the running agent is a GPT agent, the review agent should be a Claude agent. The reviewer is a command-line program, not a harness subagent: `codex exec` for GPT, `claude -p` for Claude.

Then revise the work according to the feedback provided. One review round is sufficient. After the finished implementation, any code changes should be visualized in an artifact with graphical layout showing function calls and other explanatory text, with special emphasis for any features that are still scheduled for removal later in the TASKS pipeline.

### Method B:
The current (main) agent prepares the reconstruction task and makes sure the number of instructions is no more than 1200. Otherwise, it splits the task into subunits and only proceeds with reconstructing the first subunit.

Then the main agent will launch one Claude agent and one GPT agent to each perform an independent derivation of the source code — `claude -p` and `codex exec` respectively, both with write access to their own derivation file. Once both subagents have returned, it tells each agent using resumed sessions (`codex exec resume <session-id>`) to review the other agent's work and write the review into a review file. When both agents have done so, the main agent tells the agents to revise their own work according to the other agent's review. Finally, the main agent will merge the two revised derivations into a final reconstruction.

| Artifact | Name | Writer |
|---|---|---|
| GPT derivation | `.derivations/<PACKAGE>.GPT.md` | GPT only |
| Claude derivation | `.derivations/<PACKAGE>.Claude.md` | Claude only |
| GPT review of Claude derivation | `.reviews/<PACKAGE>.review-of-Claude.md` | GPT only |
| Claude review of GPT derivation | `.reviews/<PACKAGE>.review-of-GPT.md` | Claude only |
| Merged evidence, WIZARDS.EXE | `Reference docs/DOS reconstructed/<PACKAGE>.evidence.md` | Main agent |
| Merged evidence, CASTER.EXE | `Reference docs/Caster binary/<PACKAGE>.evidence.md` | Main agent |

After the finished implementation, the reconstructed code should be visualized in an artifact with graphical layout showing function calls and other explanatory text.

## Invariants

<!-- Things that must hold, written so a test can cite one individually — this is what a `spec`-tagged suite anchors to. -->
INV-1. **Valid PMF.** Every computed distribution has probabilities in [0,1] summing to 1 within 1e-9.
   A phase that cannot fire folds its mass in at damage 0 rather than dropping it.
INV-2. **Version gating.** A control hidden for the active version cannot move a number.
INV-3. **Swap involution.** Two swaps restore the original state; one swap exchanges sides.
INV-4. **Roster soundness.** Every unit in every version's roster selects without error.
INV-5. **No console errors** during normal interaction.
INV-6. **State round-trip.** Serialize → load → serialize is a fixpoint, and Reset yields the state a
   fresh page has.

## Deliberate deviations

<!-- Knowing departures from the thing modelled. A deviation not listed here is a defect, not a design. -->
Some checks for whether a unit has ammo are replaced with a check for whether the unit has an ammo based ranged type.

- **MoM 1.31's hero magical-ranged repeat is modelled as the common case.** 1.31's gate recognises only the Caster unit flags, so a hero falls through to the ammunition branch and gets no repeat; CP 1.60 added the missing hero test. The real 1.31 gate reads an unrelated battle-unit slot and can flip either way, so the modelled outcome is the common one, not the guaranteed one.
- **Only total Damage Taken is a starting-state input.** Irrecoverable/Irreversible Damage, Undeath Damage and Bonus HP/Extra Hits are exact internal state but are not exposed on the card or matrix, which start from Regular damage with zero bonus and no explicit override.

## Architecture

<!-- The shape of the code and why it has that shape. Structure, not a tour of the modules. -->
Fail-loud on out-of-range values. Halt with an error naming the offending value, the record or file it came from, and the set that was expected.

The calculator is a single static page. No build step, no bundler, no framework, no runtime dependencies: every source loads through a plain `<script src>` tag in `index.html`. A fan with no toolchain can open it.

Results are exact distributions computed in closed form, and the state carried through an attack is a joint distribution over (damage to attacker, damage to defender), with living figure counts recomputed per cell before each phase. Phases are not independent and must not be computed separately and summed.

Stat derivation is an ordered list of individually cited steps, not formulas. Each engine write is its own step carrying its provenance citation, and the citations are checked mechanically.

`Calculator/units_<version>.js` are build products of the generators under `tools/`. A wrong value is fixed in the generator or in its source data, never in the output.

Each supported version is a first-class rule set, independently correct, and Warlord is not a flavour of CoM2. Version is a dimension of the model, not a set of conditionals added at each point of need; the latter makes "what does version Y do here" unanswerable without reading everything.

The calculation layer holds no DOM references and loads headlessly. `index.html`'s `<script>` tags are the single source manifest, and each tag's scope marks whether the source is calculation or page.

Each step in the sequence of calculating unit stats carries a **phase**: which region of the engine makes that write. Phase is a provenance label — it records where the evidence for the write was found. The chain is stored in the calculator code and for the most part corresponds to the order in which effects are applied in the binaries.

| Phase | Where it runs |
|---|---|
| **template** | Basic roster data |
| **training-time** | When the unit is trained |
| **cast-time** | Either when the unit first receives enchantments, either on the overland map or earlier in combat, or modifications to the persistent base unit that happen every time a unit performs an attack |
| **immunity** | An artificial step that strips any curses that the unit could not have received assuming it had its immunities before the curses were attempted applied |
| **a** | precalc, in the binary |
| **b** | precalc, in the early script hook |
| **c** | magic calc, in the binary |
| **d** | magic calc, in the late script hook |
| **e** | the binary's post-hook tail: the clamps, the aura pass, and the effects after them |
| **attack-specific** | not a part of calculating the unit stats shown in the UI, but steps that are conditionally run within each attack phase |

## Input/output contract

<!-- What goes in, what comes out, and what callers may rely on. -->
The user specifies the version, a roster unit or a custom unit both for the attacker and defender, and a set of enchantments and conditions for the attacker and defender.

The calculator will then show the probability mass functions for each of the damage and fear phases in the combat sequence (e.g., thrown, breath, gaze, melee, counterattack, wall of fire etc.).

Hovering a final modified value in the UI shows the complete chain that produced it: the editable base, then every applied transform with its source and running value before and after the write, and finally the displayed result. The chain follows the applicable binary/CAS execution order, not UI grouping or effect name. It must be emitted from the same ordered transform path that computes the value rather than reconstructed independently after calculation.

There is also a melee and a ranged matrix view, where the user specifies filters for which units to consider as attackers and defenders, and which enchantments and conditions are attempted applied to the attacker, defender, and globally. The matrices then show how each matchup would fare.

Every ability and enchantment control carries a tooltip describing its modelled effect.

The page keeps its full state in `localStorage` and restores it on reload; Reset returns the page to the state a fresh load has. A share link carries the same state in the URL fragment. On load a share link takes precedence over stored state, and it is one-shot: the fragment is dropped after import, so the recipient's later edits save to their own storage.

Restoring a saved state ignores a control id this build no longer has, but halts on a value outside the set its control offers. Retiring an option therefore obliges the build either to accept that older saved states stop, or to state a migration for the retired value. A state that fails to apply is discarded rather than retried: a stored blob is removed so it cannot throw on every reload, and a share link falls back to the recipient's own stored state.

## Damage calculator purpose and non-goals

<!-- What this exists to do and how a finished version would be judged good; then what it deliberately does not do. -->

The project is divided into two: A combat damage calculator and an interactive manual. Currently, only the damage calculator is under active development.

The damage calculator seeks to be a tool that fans of the 1994 game Master of Magic and its later patches and mods can use to play around with to see how well the various roster units and custom units would fare against other units. The calculator must support the application of any combination of the combat-relevant enchantments and conditions.

The supported game versions are
- Master of Magic (MoM) 1.31
- MoM 1.60
- Caster of Magic (CoM1) 6.08
- CoM for Windows (CoM2) 1.05.11
- Warlord 1.5.12.7

MoM 1.31, MoM 1.60 and CoM1 can be referred to as the "DOS versions", and CoM2 and Warlord can be referred to as "modern versions".

Game bugs are reproduced faithfully.

The ultimate source of truth for the calculator formulas and calculation sequence is the contents of the binaries, WIZARDS.EXE and CASTER.EXE. Most relevant parts of these binaries have had their source code reconstructed as part of this project. Any gaps in the reconstructed source should be filled in as part of a row in the TASKS file, using the appropriate protocol above for binary reconstruction.

The "attack" is defined as the result of one mouse click in the game on an enemy unit. One attacker against one defender. A sequence of attack phases such as breath, thrown, gaze, attack, counterattack, and a few others.

Out of scope:
- Movement
- Ammo (some binary logic tests for ammo, but this seems equivalent to testing for ranged type)
- Multi-round combat
- Positioning
- Army resolution
- Overland play
- Regeneration

The calculator representation of the unit properties should very closely match the binaries' representation of unit properties.

Likewise, the way that the calculator should calculate the effect of enchantments and conditions on unit stats should very closely follow the sequence that the binaries follow, with the addition of judgment calls we've made regarding the most likely ordering where spell casts and immunities interact. For example, a unit that has both magic immunity and mind storm marked is assumed to have had magic immunity before the mind storm spell was attempted against the unit, in which case the mind storm would fail to apply.

Generally, the calculator should assume that unit curses have succeeded their resistance roll against the unit and have successfully landed, except in cases like the above where an immunity would guarantee that a unit cannot have become affected by that curse. Resistance rolls that are part of an attack such as Poison Touch, Stoning, Death Gaze, Life Steal are modelled exactly, and resistance granted or imposed by a landed effect still modifies the stat.

Hero equipment is intended to be implemented after all other aspects of the calculator are functioning.

The calculator is considered "good" when it's user-friendly for casual and expert fans of the game, it enables them to easily compare how different units fare in combat given varying sets of enchantments and conditions, and to learn using the tooltips why the final stat values end up the way they do, by stepping through the chain of modifiers.
